comments.text: 25 of the 26 are in engine/tests/nyx and pass on the native and C backends. Not ported: values_and_programs_outlive_the_runtime_handle, which tests Rust's Rc keeping the runtime alive; in Nox the runtime is an owner, and values and programs are deleted before it. Changed: the panicking-callback test is a-failing-callback-leaves-the-runtime-usable, since Nox has no panics to catch. The two closure-drop tests check the runtime's entry count instead of a captured witness's destructor until the Nox card 'Deleting an owned callable runs the destructors of the owners moved into it' lands (fearless-hq #13).

Review fix: a value, program or host object that outlives its Runtime was a use-after-free. Runtime now keeps a RuntimeLedger that every Value and Program counts itself in, and !Runtime stops the program, naming what's still alive, instead of destroying under them. Nyx's userdata_free marks each host function and type released, and !Runtime checks Nyx let go of all of them before freeing them. Nox can't free them from that callback (fearless-hq card 'Taking back an owner handed to C as a context pointer'), so values_and_programs_outlive_the_runtime_handle is ported as the defined behaviour: values-and-programs-outliving-the-runtime-stop-the-program, plus a host-object variant, a-host-object-outliving-its-runtime-stops-the-program. A double release of a host instance is now ignored.
